Header:
Date: 2027-08-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Nexa CTO), Tom Reyes (Nexa ML), Priya Patel (Nexa DevOps), Jared Lo (Nexa Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):

Topics:

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi all, quick check-in today. we'll start with Lucas on the quantization results then status from Priya on KMS and peering.
[00:12] Lucas Park: thanks Maya. we ran int8 and int4 on the 50 eval prompts Tom supplied. int8 had a 0.7% accuracy drop on one metric, nothing above your 1% threshold. int4 showed a 3 prompt regression with some hallucination increase. details in the sheet.
[00:28] Tom Reyes: can you call out which prompts regressed? i want to inspect them for prompt brittleness.
[00:34] Lucas Park: sure  two were long-context legal-style prompts, one was an ambiguous instruction. we'll flag them and we can try more conservative quantization or selective quantization.
[00:45] Aisha Khan: so int8 is probably acceptable for us then? less risk for PHI?
[00:50] Lucas Park: likely yes; int8 gives big cost savings with minimal quality delta for most open architectures. we'll include confidence bands.
[00:58] Priya Patel: quick infra update  peering is active, i shared screenshots earlier. KMS ARN is pending, we need to confirm rotation policy with security. i'll aim to share ARN by tomorrow.
[01:12] Jared Lo: rotation policy is important for our auditors. can Redwood support automatic key rotation schedules?
[01:18] Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed keys and key rotation schedules; we'll document the exact flows in the KMS integration checklist.
[01:25] Ravi Singh: i'll attach that checklist in the notes after the call.
[01:30] Tom Reyes: about the spike behavior, when we ran the 1k-request test earlier we saw fallbacks trigger but latency was within SLO after fallback. we should run another with fallback enabled end-to-end.
[01:41] Lucas Park: agreed. we'll run a 1k spike test that simulates your 3x traffic burst and verify automatic fallback to smaller model and routing. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
[01:52] Aisha Khan: any change needed to RBAC or deploy permissions during the pilot? we want to limit who can flip models.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports RBAC; we can lock deploy permissions to a group and use SSO. we'll demo that in a short session if you want.
[02:06] Priya Patel: also, regarding egress: do you still recommend NAT for metrics export? we want to centralize egress.
[02:12] Lucas Park: for metrics export you can either allow egress to your telemetry endpoint or we can push logs into your SIEM via the peered connection. both are supported.
[02:20] Jared Lo: on audit logs, what format will you provide? our SIEM needs JSON with a timestamp field and user-id.
[02:27] Maya Chen: audit logs are JSON lines with request_id, timestamp, user, route, token_count, model_version. we'll include a sample file in the follow-up.
[02:38] Tom Reyes: small point on caching: a few of our long prompts saw quality drop after aggressive prefix eviction. can TTL be tuned per-route?
[02:45] Lucas Park: yes, caching TTL is route configurable. we usually tune TTL per workload to avoid stale prefixes causing hallucinations. we'll propose TTL settings in the benchmarking notes.
[02:55] Maya Chen: great  sounds like concrete progress. quick recap: Lucas will publish quant results and spreadsheet; Priya to send KMS ARN and rotation policy; Tom and Lucas to run the spike test; Maya to share SOC2 link and audit sample.
[03:12] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone, appreciate the progress.

End of call.
